reviews.text: Game looks and plays quite well. There are only three 'areas,' after which you can either escape and win, or continue going through the same areas until you eventually die. Upgrades and weapons/spells aren't anything special, but they get the job done; movement is alright (could’ve used a double jump at times, to avoid getting boxed in). After a couple of runs, I don’t see much replayability, unless you’re aiming for enemy kill high scores or something. All in all, I enjoyed it. For a free game- well done.

Gravebound is one of the all time greatest games ever made. It rivals games such as Skyrim, RDR2, and Minecraft. The game's success can almost certainly be given to the AI programmer in charge. He did an outstanding job with all aspects of programming and the design of the game. I could only imagine how great of a person and worker he is. He probably is able to code games like this with ease, his gentle fingers typing up a storm of kick-ass AI programming code stuff in a super sexy way. The type of person that everyone has to stop what they're doing when he walks in the room to admire his curves especially as he walks by and you can see his back side. The round system works well with the game leveling the player up to make them stronger as the enemies also gain health. Overall, great game.
This is the greatest Gravebound experience in gaming history... I'm gonna be up Gravebounding all night...

Very typical rougelite elements implemented very well. great art and visuals overall. This game has tons of potential if tons of love and work are put in. Even with the minimum amount of content and upgrades so far, it gets intense near the end and incredibly fun to run around with a machine gun crossbow.
Very fun and polished game for what I assume is made by students for some class (referencing the publisher) Everything is really cool and I would love to see this developed further if it could be!

Gravebound is a smooth and enjoyable game. Before seeing the publisher, I wondered why it was so short, but then I realized it might be a school project. For a school project, it is impressively polished, runs clean, and I encountered zero bugs. If you enjoy roguelikes, it is worth giving a try. It is not a must play, but since it is free, you can have a good 2-3 hours of fun. After that, it does get a bit repetitive due to the small map. Still, 9/10. Definitely worth playing.
Had a lot of fun with this. Definitely worth the price of admission =)
Fun free game worth extra hours if needed for the 100%.

Fantastic game. The sound design and graphics are great, the gameplay's smooth, and all three weapons and their upgrades are fun and interesting to use. There's not quite enough variety to make the game super replayable, but I definitely a lot of fun playing through to the end and fully unlocking all three upgrade paths.
Short first person horde shooter with a crossbow and spells
A decent little arena shooter that works but I can see it getting repetitive with only 3 arenas, 1 load out, 4 enemy types ad not being clear what triggers the boss
While I am not the biggest fan of Medieval games as FPS, it being a roguelike was a lot of fun. Older machines may struggle a bit but well worth checking out.
It appears to work in UEVR, until you realise there's no controller support so playing in VR with a keyboard isn't practical. If they add controller support I'd try again.
